newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Handlowy 96 net up 26.1 pct to PLN 530 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Handlowy 96 net up 26.1 pct to PLN 530 mln.

text.p: The net profit of Poland's largest commercial Bank Handlowy SA, slated for flotation in Warsaw and on a foreign bourse in mid-year, rose 26.1 percent in 1996 to 530.42 million zlotys ($172.8 million), the bank's president said.
"In terms of financial results it was the best year in the history of Bank Handlowy," Cezary Stypulkowski told a news confernce on Wednesday.
He said the bank's revenue came mainly from interest and foreign exchange opertions, but noted that their growth was slowing while more and more cash came from securities operations and commission.
Stypulkowski said that out of the net profit the bank would pay out 215 million zlotys in dividend to its owner, the treasury, and allot 106 million zlotys for reserve capital.
He said the net profit figure was revised down from previously reported preliminary figure of 555 million after the bank created a provision for future privatisation costs.

He also said the bank would use the 1996 earnings to finance an issue of convertible bonds exchangable into 30 percent of the bank's equity at their nominal value of four zlotys each, to be given to to-be-created pension funds.

"The bonds, with a likely maturity of 10-years, will not bear any interest coupon and will have all the features of shares, including rights to take up new stock isuues and to dividend," Stypulkowski said.

The sale of the bank originally assumed that 30 percent of its shares would be offered to institutional investors, 30 percent would be sold in a public offering and 30 percent given to the pension funds. Employees would get five percent and the treasury would keep five percent.

The government decided however, to give the funds convertible bonds rather than shares which entailed changes in the sizes of the original stock tranches to keep the rations unchanged after the bonds are converted into stock.
Both institutional and public offering tranches were raised to 42.9 percent while stakes for employees and the treasury rose to 7.1 percent.
Stypulkowski said Handlowy's balance sheet total rose 47.8 percent to 14.68 billion zlotys in 1996, boosted mainly by increased credit action and activity on capital markets.
He also said Handlowy serviced 70 out of Poland's 100 biggest companies in terms of revenue and 53 percent of the country's 500 largest firms.
The volume of foreign exchange transactions cleared by the bank rose 5.6 percent to $17.5 billion last year, securing it the position of forex market leader.

Stypulkowski said Handlowy's return on equity in 1996 was 31.7 percent while return on assets was 4.3 percent. The bank's capital adequacy ratio was 16.6 percent against the central bank's requirement of eight percent.
Handlowy's capital was at 1.85 billion zlotys in 1996.
